previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis and recent Puestow procedure was readmitted for worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. He reported a syncopal episode possibly related to pain, initially concerning for seizure but determined to be a pseudoseizure. CT imaging showed expected post-surgical changes without abscess, mild colonic wall thickening of uncertain significance, and a trace pericardial effusion. He was managed medically with IV pain control and antiemetics, advanced to a regular diet, and remained stable. Wound cultures grew Staphylococcus aureus and Group B Streptococcus, interpreted as skin flora without evidence of infection. He improved clinically and was discharged home with oral pain medication and follow-up plans. No surgical intervention was required.

Brief Hospital Course:
#. Syncope: Patient reported a history of multiple episodes of 
syncope for the last few weeks and most or all of them are

work up was not pursued at the time as it had been done in the 
past. These episodes were thought to be vagally mediated syncope 
in the setting of intense pain. He was ruled out for MI w/ 3(-) 
CE's and telemetry did not reveal any arrhythmias.

#. Acute on chronic pancreatitis: Patient with a history of 
pancreatitis and presented with ~2 weeks of abdominal pain, N/V 
and inability to take PO for 3 days. His symptoms consistent 
with previous episodes of pancreatitis. He was kept NPO, given 
IVF, pain medication and antiemetic medication. On HD2 his 
condition was much improved, his diet advanced to clears and 
pain medication changed to PO. He wished to be discharged that 
day as he felt much better and given that he tolerated his diet 
he was discharged later in the afternoon.

#. Chest pain: Patient presented with 3 days of atypical chest 
pain. EKG was unchanged from baseline and trop (-) x3. Pain is 
likely associated with his abdominal process.

#. Elevated lactate: Patient had an elevated lactate with an AG 
of 24 in the ED. His lactate decreased to normal levels (1.9) 
and AG to 12 after IVF. AG was 9 on the day of discharge.

#. Seizure vs Pseudoseizure: No seizure activity during his 
hospitalization.

#. HTN: Continued home meds.

#. DM II: Metformin was held while inpatient and ISS started. He 
was instructed to re-start metformin as an outpatient.
